chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me:

'Write and transmit your knowledge among your brethren. If you die, then bequeath your books to your sons. For there will come upon the people a time of commotion (harj) in which they will find no comfort except in their books.'

key_terms.بُثَّ: transmit/spread — disseminate actively among others, not merely conserve privately
key_terms.عِلْمَكَ: your knowledge — the sacred learning that must be preserved and actively transmitted
key_terms.هَرْجٍ: commotion/turmoil — an eschatological term denoting widespread civil strife and chaos at the end of times
key_terms.يَأْنَسُونَ: they find comfort — from ʾanisa, to feel intimate familiarity and solace with something

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about writing and preserving Islamic knowledge for times of tribulation?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) commands his close companion al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar to write down and actively disseminate knowledge, and to preserve it for future generations by bequeathing his books to his sons. He grounds this command in an eschatological warning: a time of widespread turmoil (harj) will come when written books become humanity's sole refuge and source of spiritual solace.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid Al Barqy, from one of his companions, from Abu Saeed Al Khaybari, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me:

‘Write and transmit your knowledge among your brethren. So if you were to die, so leave your books as an inheritance, for there would be coming a time of commotion upon the people, they would not be finding comfort (during) in it but except with your books’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from certain persons of his people from abu Sa‘id al-Khaybari from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following. “Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said,

‘You must write down (Hadith) and spread your knowledge among your brethren. If you will die your children will inherit your books. A time will come when people will face chaos and they will find no comfort but with their books.’”
